thesis: The wealth-path framework distinguishes whose capital is used and whose business is owned or operated.
summary: The reviewed passages classify bootstrapping, raising capital, investing, and fund management using two ownership dimensions. Raising capital involves selling a share of the company; investing and fund management concern interests in other businesses. This is an organizing model, not an assessment of suitability, expected returns, or the full regulatory obligations of any route.
